questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good university with a course catalouge that offered courses not offered at home or courses at a higher level than at home. The nice weather in Santa Barbara didnt hurt my opinion of it either though.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The compulsory orientations they charged us for were completely unnecessary as everything was straightforward from regular student resources, so maybe cancel that and save everyone the 75 bucks.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several compulsory orientations with reduntant information. The only upside was meeting some of the other exchangers because everyone had to go.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As the exchangers had lower priority in housing than any other students mostly triples were available and only in the building furthest from campus. Otherwise not that bad though.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: rudimentary kitchen without any kitchenware in the apartements. Good help was available for finding "cheaper" groceries, which helped a little but cold by no means even out the local grocery prices compared to almost everywhere else. Cooking yourself was still better than overpriced mediocore food from dining halls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its cramped, the ebds are uncomfortable and the experience hinges mostly on the chance of getting nice and cleanly roommates as there is no privacy in the campus housing apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Annoying from abroad, as course information is often scarse or simply unavailable and requires a lot of research, but straightforward locally with input of classmates.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course website after past times for signup, but barely anything before that, as the course catalouge lacks regularity, so having a plan b and c is adviseable.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: got everything i wanted and knew existed but missed out on one course i wouldve loved to take, because it wasnt advertised on the course website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If possible contact students from your own major who have attended the same university or local staff to help find courses youre interested in as especially courses on other majors are often difficult to find.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Difficult, as the level of teaching is generally lower and there is less focus on assisting in learning but academic expectations are higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Night and day. UCPH has more focus on learning through lectures and learning to apply knowledge through ta classes, which are two things that were nearly totally absent at ucsb. Learning happens on own time here and lectures only give overviews and ta classes dont actually aim at teaching you to apply your knowledge even if they are available. Office hours are a nice concept here but in practice often tedious because of some professors lack of interest in teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Math 111A - Abstract algebra
Phys 123A - Condensed matter
phys 141 - optics
cmpsc 190H - Quantum Algorithm
phys 132 - stellar structure and evolution
phys 129L - intro to scientific computing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
190H is a difficult but rewarding course with a great professor that aims at preparing students for research. 
132 is nice, because it is not heavy on rigor.
123a was interesting but mathematically challenging and took up a lot of time

questions.answer: groceries are twice as expensive as they are back home. Travelling by train probably 4 times as expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Gas is cheap, which is only relevant if you get a car

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: hiking trips, road trips, a lot of cheap travel opportunities to mexico or hawaii independently or with friends

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: seeing the national parks as there are a lot of unique places in california that are nothing like anything at home.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: local state parks, hiking trails, wineries, LA if one is into big cities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: somewhat easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: people are more outgoing and put a way bigger emphasis on spending time together

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the social stuff

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: do a roadtrip, talk to the local students and join in club activity on campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: mind the alcohol laws. Its different from back home and they dont mess around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends we made along the way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: workload in classes to not fall behind because of mismatched quarter schedules compared to back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
